name: mergesort_missing_taskwait
task: This project sorts a large integer array with a task-parallel merge sort, split across multiple translation units: include/data_gen.h + src/data_gen.cpp (a deterministic random-array generator and a sortedness check), include/merge.h + src/merge.cpp (the sequential merge step and a sequential merge sort used for small ranges), include/sort.h + src/sort.cpp (merge_sort_serial() and the OpenMP task-based merge_sort_parallel(), with the sequential cutoff constant kTaskCutoff), and src/main.cpp (the profiling entry point). merge_sort_parallel() opens '#pragma omp parallel' / '#pragma omp single' and sort_with_tasks() recursively creates two '#pragma omp task' children for the two halves, but it then calls merge_ranges() immediately without waiting for the children. The tasks are only queued at that point, so the merge runs on halves that are still unsorted (and afterwards races with the children writing the same ranges), and the output is not sorted. Fix sort_with_tasks() in src/sort.cpp so merge_sort_parallel() always returns exactly the sorted sequence for every input size, content and number of threads, while keeping the recursion task-parallel with OpenMP (do not simply remove the task pragmas or call std::sort / the serial sort for the whole array; keep the kTaskCutoff sequential cutoff). Do not change any function signature declared in include/sort.h, include/merge.h or include/data_gen.h.
notes: build_command compiles the profiling entry point at build/app (src/main.cpp -> data_gen.cpp, merge.cpp, sort.cpp). This binary must be built and then executed via run_command to drive DiscoPoP's instrumentation and produce its dynamic profiling output, including dynamic_dependencies, over the recursive task creation in sort_with_tasks(). test_command builds and runs a separate correctness harness at build/run_tests (from tests/test_main.cpp); it is independent of the profiling binary and should not be used as the DiscoPoP execution target. Both binaries link the same data_gen.cpp, merge.cpp, sort.cpp object files, so no separate CMake/Meson/etc. configuration is required — plain 'make' is sufficient to build, run, and test.
